short_statement: A recent preprint gives a superconstant additive configuration-LP gap for bin packing; the exact growth remains undetermined.
full_statement: An instance of one-dimensional bin packing consists of item sizes $s_1,\ldots,s_n\in(0,1]$ and unit-capacity bins. A configuration is a multiset of items whose total size is at most $1$. The Gilmore-Gomory configuration LP has one nonnegative variable $x_C$ for each feasible configuration $C$ and minimizes $\sum_C x_C$ subject to covering each item type in the required multiplicity. Equivalently, in the high-multiplicity view, each column records how many items of each size appear in one bin. Let $OPT_f(I)$ be the fractional optimum and $OPT(I)$ be the integer optimum. Define $G(B)=\sup\{OPT(I)-OPT_f(I):OPT_f(I)\le B\}$. The quantitative problem is to determine the asymptotic growth of $G(B)$ as $B$ grows. The historical question asked whether $G(B)$ is bounded by a universal constant. The stronger historical Modified Integer Round-Up Property predicts $OPT(I)\le \lceil OPT_f(I)\rceil+1$ for every instance. The known upper bound is logarithmic in $OPT_f(I)$, and the new superconstant lower bound is recorded below.
background: Bin packing and cutting stock are core problems in approximation algorithms, integer programming, and operations research. The configuration LP is unusually strong: although it has exponentially many columns, it captures the natural pattern structure of bins and underlies the Karmarkar-Karp approximation scheme. Most approximation questions ask for multiplicative ratios, but this problem asks for an additive constant, which is much sharper and directly relevant in large cutting-stock instances where a few extra bins matter. The problem is also connected to discrepancy theory: rounding a fractional collection of configurations to integer bins is a vector-balancing problem with additional packing structure. Hoberg and Rothvoss's logarithmic bound shows that discrepancy methods go far, but their own framing indicates that further progress likely needs more algebraic or structural use of bin-packing configurations.
known_results:
Rebecca Hoberg and Thomas Rothvoss give an $O(\log OPT_f)$ additive upper bound for the configuration LP.

Ilan Doron-Arad, 'Additive Omega(log* OPT) Gap for Bin Packing with Three Items per Bin' (arXiv:2611.09447v1, 2026), Theorem 1.3, gives an $\Omega(\log^* OPT)$ gap with sizes arbitrarily close to $1/3$. This builds on the September OpenAI construction. Theorem 1.2 also transfers arbitrary instances' gaps to this restricted class up to constants.

Theorem 1.1 separately rules out deterministic polynomial-time additive error $o(\log^* OPT)$ unless $P=NP$. This computational hardness is distinct from the unconditional LP-gap claim.

If correct, the construction refutes both a constant additive gap and MIRUP. The iterated-logarithmic lower bound and logarithmic upper bound still differ. The proof and dependency chain have not been independently certified here.
open_problem: Determine the sharp growth of $G(B)$ between the reported iterated-logarithmic lower bound and logarithmic upper bound. The historical constant-gap question has a reported negative resolution.

progress.summary: Doron-Arad (2026) quantifies the superconstant gap as $\Omega(\log^* OPT)$, even near item size $1/3$; the growth rate remains open.

links.title: Additive Omega(log* OPT) Gap for Bin Packing with Three Items per Bin

counterexample_rationale: A refutation of constant gap could be given by explicit item-size families and certified LP/integer optima. Even small high-gap examples are machine-checkable with integer programming and column generation.
alphaevolve_rationale: Automated search can generate item-size multisets, solve or approximate the configuration LP, and look for fractional structures with large additive gaps. Search may also discover rounding patterns suggesting a proof.

literature.synthesis: Earlier discrepancy results primarily improved upper bounds or limited rounding techniques. The new result claims an actual integrality-gap family, changing the qualitative answer while leaving quantitative growth undetermined.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Check the new construction and its LP convention before searching for improved gap families or rounding bounds.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: Certify integer and fractional objectives using the same configuration convention. Separate the unconditional gap claim from computational hardness and from restrictions on rounding algorithms.
